issues.description: Stock.findStockIngredient is specified as findStockIngredient(String) in the problem statement/UML, but the template provides only findStockIngredient(String, boolean caseSensitive) and therefore does not match the required one-parameter API. This forces students to either change the template API or to implement SealSaloon against a different method signature than the one described.
issues.suggestedFix: Add/replace the template method with `public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name)` to match the specification. If case sensitivity is desired as an extension, keep `findStockIngredient(String, boolean)` as an overload, but ensure the one-parameter method exists and is the primary one referenced.

issues.description: The specification is inconsistent about SealSaloon.stock: it first describes it as a `final Stock stock` instance field initialized in the constructor, but later explicitly requires the `stock` attribute to be static (shared across all instances). This leaves students unclear whether to implement an instance-level `final` field or a `static final` field.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the statement consistent by choosing one design and reflecting it everywhere: either require `private static final Stock stock = new Stock();` (and remove the 'final instance field initialized in constructor' wording), or require `private final Stock stock;` (and remove the requirement that stock is static).

issues.description: The UML lists SealSaloon.calculateTotalPrice(Meal) and SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery(String,int,int) as instance methods, but the problem statement explicitly requires both methods to be static (because they operate on shared stock). This mismatch can cause students to implement non-static methods that fail against expectations/tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the UML to mark `acceptSupplyDelivery` and `calculateTotalPrice` as static (e.g., `{static}` or underlined), and align the UML’s depiction of `stock` accordingly, so diagram and text do not contradict.
